title: Counting the Months an Amount Has Stood Overdue
content:
# Counting the Months an Amount Has Stood Overdue

The months overdue on a project under Equipment Replacement & Retrofit Projects are counted in three different ways, according to how long the amount has been standing.

## Rule

Where the amount has stood overdue for 60 days or more, each month or part month begun counts as a whole month, a month being 30 days.

Where the amount has stood overdue for more than 30 days but fewer than 60, the months overdue are counted pro rata by the day, as the days overdue divided by thirty and taken to two decimal places.

Where the amount has stood overdue for 30 days or fewer, the months overdue are counted as one month, that is as 1 month.

## Both sides of each boundary

| Days overdue | How counted | Months overdue |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | as one month | 1 |
| 30 | as one month | 1 |
| 31 | pro rata, 31 divided by thirty | 1.03 |
| 45 | pro rata, 45 divided by thirty | 1.5 |
| 59 | pro rata, 59 divided by thirty | 1.97 |
| 60 | each month or part month begun | 2 |
| 61 | each month or part month begun | 3 |
| 90 | each month or part month begun | 3 |

Exactly 30 days is 30 days or fewer and is counted as one month; 31 days is more than 30 and is counted pro rata; exactly 60 days is 60 days or more and counts the months begun, which at 60 days is two.

## Worked counts (hypothetical)

An amount standing 45 days overdue is counted at 1.5 months; the same amount standing 61 days overdue has begun a third thirty-day month and is counted at 3 months.
